title: Hertz line contact on hex20 faces: a cylinder pressed on a flat (implicit mortar contact on curved quadratic faces)
source: H. Hertz, Über die Berührung fester elastischer Körper, J. reine angew. Math. 92:156–171, 1882; K. L. Johnson, Contact Mechanics, Cambridge University Press 1985, §4.3 (two-dimensional contact of cylindrical bodies): b = √(4PR/(πE*)), p₀ = 2P/(πb), with 1/E* = 2(1 − ν²)/E for two bodies of one material and R the cylinder's radius on a flat; outside the contact the gap h(x) = (b²/2R)[(x/b)√(x²/b² − 1) − ln(x/b + √(x²/b² − 1))], the integral of the slope √(x² − b²)/R that the elliptical pressure leaves

quantities.quantity: the largest contact pressure p₀ (at x = 0)
quantities.reason: p₀ = 2P/(πb) for the load per length P = 2265.57 N/mm, b = 0.5 mm; the contact width spans three or four hex20 faces of the graded mesh, and the largest nodal pressure is compared (corner and mid-side pressures alternate a little around the ellipse)

quantities.quantity: the force across the contact (half model, 1 mm thick)
quantities.reason: the pressure carries the whole load; the soft springs that hold the indenter before contact take a millionth

quantities.quantity: the gap at the secondary node at x = 0.42285 (0.85 b, inside the contact)
quantities.reason: within the half-width the surfaces touch: the last node before b is closed (the next node, at x = 0.514 > b, is open), so the contact's edge lies between them, as b = 0.5 says

quantities.quantity: the contact pressure at the secondary node at x = 0.71946 (1.44 b)
quantities.reason: outside the contact there is no pressure (the nodes of the faces that hold the contact's edge, up to x = 0.605, carry part of the last closed node's pressure)

quantities.quantity: the gap at the secondary node at x = 0.71946 (1.44 b, outside the contact)
quantities.reason: Hertz's separation beyond b; the foundation is ten half-widths wide and deep, not a half-plane, and the coarse faces round off the contact's edge
